aligned.en: He laid it down that prayer should weigh heavily upon a person, and that he should reckon it as one who has been assigned a task to perform and seeks to be relieved of it.

aligned.en: He said: "Know what to answer" concerning the heretics among the [gentile] religious communities, and how to debate them and reply to them should they raise objections against you.

aligned.ja: וקאלוא לא שנו אלא אפיקורוס גוי אבל אפיקורוס ישראל כל שכן דפקר, יעני אנה יתזיד אסתכ'פאפא והזוא, ולד'לך לא ינבגי מחאורתה ראסא לאנה לא ינג'בר ולא טב פיה ראסא, כל באיה לא ישובון ולא ישיגו ארחות חיים.
aligned.en: They said: "They taught this only of an Epicurean who is a gentile, but an Epicurean who is an Israelite—all the more so does he deny" (BT Sanhedrin 38b)—meaning that such a one only grows more brazen in his contempt and mockery. For this reason one ought not engage him in disputation at all, since he is past mending and there is no remedy for him whatsoever: "none who go to her return, nor do they reach the paths of life" (Prov 2:19).

aligned.ja: וקאל פמע כונך תתעלם ארא אלמלל לתעלם כיף תרד עליהם אחד'ר אן יעלק בבאלך שי מן ד'לך, ואעלם אן אלד'י תכ'דם בין ידיה יעלם סראירך והו קולה ודע לפני מי אתה עמל.
aligned.en: And he said: even while you study the doctrines of the [gentile] communities so as to learn how to refute them, beware lest anything of that cling to your mind. And know that the One before whom you serve knows your innermost secrets—this is his saying, "and know before whom you toil."

pairs.en: you study the doctrines of the [gentile] communities
to learn how to refute them

aligned.en: Mishnah [18]

aligned.ja: הד'א מת'ל ען קצר אלעמר, וכת'רהֵ אלעלם, וכסל אלנאס ען טלבה, מע כת'רהֵ אלאג'ר עליה, ומע חץ' אלשריעה ותאכידהא פי אלטלב ואלתעלם.
aligned.en: This is a parable concerning the brevity of life, the abundance of knowledge to be acquired, and people's sloth in pursuing it—despite the great reward for it, and despite the Torah's urging and its insistence upon its pursuit and study.

aligned.ja: משנה [א]
aligned.en: Mishnah [1]

aligned.ja: הד'א אלתאמל יוג'ב לאלאנסאן אלתואצ'ע בנט'רה מאין בא. ותאמלה מאלה יוג'ב לה אלתהאון במתאע אלדניא.
aligned.en: This reflection imposes humility upon a person—by his considering whence he came. His reflecting upon where he is going imposes upon him contempt for the goods of this world.

pairs.en: This reflection imposes humility upon a person
by his considering whence he came
His reflecting upon where he is going
contempt for the goods of this world

aligned.ja: ותאמלה לעט'מהֵ אלאמר יוג'ב לה אלמבאדרה לאמתת'אל אמרה. ואד'א חצלת הד'ה אלת'לאת' אשיא פלא ד'נב ראסא.
aligned.en: And his reflecting upon the greatness of the Matter imposes upon him eagerness to comply with His command. When these three things are attained, there is no sin at all.

pairs.en: his reflecting upon the greatness of the Matter
eagerness to comply with His command

aligned.en: Mishnah [2]

aligned.ja: יעני לולא כ'וף אלסלטאן בלענא בעצ'נא בעץ' אחיא.
aligned.en: He means: were it not for fear of the government, we would have swallowed one another alive.

aligned.ja: משנה [ג]
aligned.en: Mishnah [3]

aligned.ja: דלילה עלי אן מושב לצים יתסמי כל מג'לס לא יתכלם פיה פי פצ'ילהֵ אלתורה מן אכ'ר אלפסוק אלד'י קאל כי אם בתורת ה' חפצו, כאנה יקול למא כאן חפצו בתורת ה' לם יג'לס במושב לצים אלד'י ליס פיה תורת ה'.
aligned.en: His proof that any gathering in which words concerning the excellence of the Torah are not spoken is called "a session of scoffers" derives from the end of the verse that says, "but his delight is in the Torah of the Lord" (Ps 1:2). It is as though he were saying: since his delight was in the Torah of the Lord, he did not sit in a session of scoffers, in which there is no Torah of the Lord.

pairs.en: is called "a session of scoffers"

pairs.ja: לא יתכלם פיה פי פצ'ילהֵ אלתורה
pairs.en: words concerning the excellence of the Torah are not spoken
but his delight is in the Torah of the Lord
he did not sit in a session of scoffers

aligned.ja: ושרח וידם מן אלכלאם אלכ'פי מן קולה דממה דקה, ומן ד'לך שרח אלתרגום וידם אהרן ושבח אהרן.
aligned.en: And his interpretation of *wa-yiddom* ["and he was silent"] as belonging to the category of faint speech derives from the phrase "a thin, faint sound" (1 Kgs 19:12); and from this too is the interpretation of the Targum's rendering of "and Aaron was silent" (Lev 10:3) as "and Aaron praised."

pairs.en: as belonging to the category of faint speech
a thin, faint sound

pairs.en: the interpretation of the Targum's rendering of "and Aaron was silent"

aligned.ja: ודלילה עלי אנה כמת'ל מן חמל ג'מלהֵ אלשריעה מן קולה נטל עליו, כאן נזול אלשרע כלה עליה פקט הו.
aligned.en: And his proof that [the one who studies Torah] is like one who has borne the whole burden of the Law derives from the phrase "[a portion] was set upon him"—as though the descent of the entire Law had been upon him alone.

pairs.en: like one who has borne the whole burden of the Law
[a portion] was set upon him

aligned.ja: משנה [ד]
aligned.en: Mishnah [4]

aligned.ja: זבחי מתים, תתסמי תקרובת עבודה זרה כמא סמאהא אלנץ עלי מא בינא פי ת'אלת' עבודה זרה. וסמאהא איצ'א קיא צואה תהג'ין להא כמא יסמי עבודה זרה נפסהא גלולים ושקוצים.
aligned.en: "Sacrifices of the dead" (Ps 106:28) is a designation for an idolatrous offering, just as Scripture named it so, according to what we explained in the third chapter of [tractate] Avodah Zarah. He also named it "vomit and filth" as a way of disparaging it, just as idolatry itself is called "dung-idols" and "abominations."

pairs.en: Sacrifices of the dead
an idolatrous offering
we explained in the third chapter of [tractate] Avodah Zarah
He also named it "vomit and filth"
called "dung-idols" and "abominations."

aligned.ja: ותקדם קבל הד'א אלפסוק פסוק ידל עלי אלאשתגאל באלאכל ואלשרב ותרך אלתורה ואלתפקה פיהא, ולד'לך צארת אלשלחנות כלהא כאנהא אנמא יוכל עליהא אלקד'אראת ואלאוסאך' יעני מטאעם אלצנם והו קולה קבל הד'א אלפסוק וגם אלה ביין שגו ובשכר תעו כהן ונביא שגו בשכר נבלעו מן היין תעו מן השכר שגו בראה פקו פליליה כי כל שלחנות וכו'.
aligned.en: Before this verse there comes a verse indicating preoccupation with eating and drinking and the abandonment of the Torah and of intelligent reflection upon it; for this reason all the "tables" become as though nothing were eaten upon them but filth and refuse—that is, the foods [offered to] the idol. This is his statement before this verse: "But these too reel with wine and stagger with strong drink: priest and prophet reel with strong drink, they are confused by wine, they stagger from strong drink, they reel in vision, they totter in judgment; for all tables [are covered with vomit and filth]" (Isa 28:7–8).

pairs.en: preoccupation with eating and drinking
the abandonment of the Torah and of intelligent reflection upon it
all the "tables"
filth and refuse
the foods [offered to] the idol

pairs.ja: וגם אלה ביין שגו ובשכר תעו
pairs.en: these too reel with wine and stagger with strong drink

aligned.ja: משנה [ה]
aligned.en: Mishnah [5]

aligned.ja: קאל חנניה בן חכינאי אלד'י ינתבה באלליל מן נומה ויסיר פי אלטריק פראדא והו יפכר פי תעטיל אלדין קד אסתוג'ב אלעקובה מן ענד אללה.
aligned.en: Rabbi Ḥananyah ben Ḥakhinai said: one who wakes in the night from his sleep and travels along the road alone while pondering the neglect of religion has made himself deserving of punishment from God.

pairs.en: wakes in the night from his sleep

aligned.ja: משנה [ו]
aligned.en: Mishnah [6]

aligned.ja: עול תורה, אלתזאם אלקראה, ועול מלכות, כלף אלסלטאן וג'ורה. ועול דרך ארץ, כלף אלזמאן, יקול אן באג'ר אלתזאמה לעול תורה יכפיה אללה לואזם אלמלוך ויסהל עליה פי כלף אלזמאן.
aligned.en: "The yoke of Torah" [means] the obligation of [Torah] study; "the yoke of government," the burdens of the ruler and his oppression; and "the yoke of worldly affairs," the burdens of the age. He says that in return for taking upon himself the yoke of Torah, God spares him the demands of kings and eases for him the burdens of the age.

pairs.en: "The yoke of Torah" [means] the obligation of [Torah] study
"the yoke of government," the burdens of the ruler and his oppression
"the yoke of worldly affairs,"

aligned.ja: וקאלוא פורק עול האומר תורה מן השמים ואיני סובלה. וקאלוא חרות על הלוחות חירות על הלוחות, יעני אלחריה מן נואיב אלדהר ונואיב אלסלטאן למן אמתת'אל אלשי אלמנצוץ עלי אללוחות.
aligned.en: And they said: "Whoever casts off the yoke—he who says, 'The Torah is from Heaven and I will not bear it'" [is removed from this and from that]. And they said: "Read not *ḥarut* ['engraved'] upon the tablets but *ḥerut* ['freedom'] upon the tablets" (BT Eruvin 54a)—meaning freedom from the calamities of time and the calamities of the ruler for whoever complies with what is set down upon the tablets.

pairs.ja: חרות על הלוחות חירות על הלוחות
pairs.en: Read not *ḥarut* ['engraved'] upon the tablets but *ḥerut* ['freedom'] upon the tablets

aligned.ja: משנה [ז]
aligned.en: Mishnah [7]

aligned.ja: בינא פי אול סנהדרין אן עדה לא יקע עלי אקל מן עשרה. והנאך בינא אן בית דין לא יכון אקל מן שלשה והם אלד'ין יתסמון אלהים למעני אלחכם.
aligned.en: We explained at the beginning of Sanhedrin that the term "congregation" does not apply to fewer than ten. And there we explained that a court is no fewer than three—these being the ones called *elohim* in the sense of "judge."

pairs.en: We explained at the beginning of Sanhedrin

pairs.ja: עדה לא יקע עלי אקל מן עשרה
pairs.en: the term "congregation" does not apply to fewer than ten

pairs.ja: בית דין לא יכון אקל מן שלשה
pairs.en: a court is no fewer than three
the ones called *elohim* in the sense of "judge."

aligned.ja: ושרח אגודה, קבצ'ה, ואליד פיה כ'מסהֵ אצאבע אלד'י בה יקבץ', וג'מע אלכ'מס אצאבע יתסמי קבצ'ה איצ'א.
aligned.en: As for the interpretation of *agudah*, it is "a grasp"; the hand has within it five fingers with which one grasps, and the assembling of the five fingers is likewise called a "grasp."

pairs.en: the interpretation of *agudah*, it is "a grasp"
the hand has within it five fingers

aligned.ja: משנה [יא]
aligned.en: Mishnah [11]

aligned.ja: הד'א שי מג'מע עליה מן אלפלאספה איצ'א, אן תעויד אלפצ'איל אד'א תקדם אלעלם חתי תחצל לה מלכה קויה ת'ם תעלם אלחכמה בעד ד'לך אלתי תחט'ה עלי תלך אלכ'יראת זאד גבטה באלחכמה ומחבה פיהא וחרץ עלי אלתזייד מנהא, אד' תחרכה אלי מא אעתאד.
aligned.en: This is a matter agreed upon by the philosophers as well: that if the habituation to the virtues precedes [the acquisition of] knowledge—until a strong disposition is formed in a person—and he afterward learns the wisdom that urges him toward those goods, then his delight in wisdom, his love of it, and his striving to increase it all grow, since it moves him toward what he has grown accustomed to.

pairs.en: agreed upon by the philosophers
the habituation to the virtues
until a strong disposition
he afterward learns the wisdom
that urges him toward those goods
his delight in wisdom, his love of it
it moves him toward what he has grown accustomed to

aligned.ja: ואן תקדמת מלכאת אלשרור ת'ם תעלם בעד ד'לך וצארת אלחכמה תמנעה ממא יהואה באלעאדה ת'קלת עליה ואטרחהא.
aligned.en: But if the dispositions of the vices precede, and he afterward learns, so that wisdom comes to restrain him from what he desires by habit, then it weighs heavily upon him and he casts it off.

pairs.en: the dispositions of the vices precede
wisdom comes to restrain him from what he desires by habit
it weighs heavily upon him and he casts it off

aligned.ja: משנה [יג]
aligned.en: Mishnah [13]

aligned.ja: יקול אן הד'ה אלאשיא תבטל פצ'ילהֵ אלאנסאן אלי אן יכ'רג' מן אלעאלם והו כ'אסרא.
aligned.en: He says that these things nullify a person's virtue, so that he departs from the world a loser.

pairs.en: nullify a person's virtue
he departs from the world a loser

aligned.ja: משנה [יד]
aligned.en: Mishnah [14]

aligned.ja: מלבין פני חברו, מן יכ'ג'ל צאחבה ויכלחה. ומגלה פנים בתורה, הו אלד'י יתעדי עלי שראיע אלתורה משהר באעלאן והי גאיהֵ אלכפר כמא קאל תעלי והנפש אשר תעשה ביד רמה וכו'. ומעני מגלה פנים, יכשף וג'הה ויתקח.
aligned.en: "One who whitens the face of his fellow" [means] one who shames his companion and makes him pale. "And one who is brazen-faced toward the Torah" is the one who transgresses the statutes of the Torah, notorious and openly defiant—and this is the height of denial, as He, exalted, said: "But the person who acts with a high hand" (Num 15:30). The meaning of "brazen-faced" is one who uncovers his face and is impudent.

pairs.en: One who whitens the face of his fellow
one who shames his companion and makes him pale
one who is brazen-faced toward the Torah

pairs.ja: יתעדי עלי שראיע אלתורה משהר באעלאן
pairs.en: transgresses the statutes of the Torah, notorious and openly defiant
the height of denial
But the person who acts with a high hand
one who uncovers his face and is impudent

aligned.ja: והד'א נצהם פי שרח ד'לך והו פי גמר פאה קאלוא מגלה פנים בתורה העובר על דברי תורה בפרהסיא כיהויקים בן יאשיהו, מפר ברית זה המושך לו ערלה, והו אלד'י לם יכ'תתן פי כברה אד'א לם יכ'תתן פי צגרה.
aligned.en: This is their text in interpreting it, in [tractate] Gemar Peʾah; they said: "'One who is brazen-faced toward the Torah'—this is one who transgresses the words of Torah in public, like Jehoiakim son of Josiah; 'who breaks the covenant'—this is one who draws his foreskin over himself," that is, one who was not circumcised in his maturity if he was not circumcised in his youth.

pairs.en: their text in interpreting it
[tractate] Gemar Peʾah

pairs.ja: העובר על דברי תורה בפרהסיא כיהויקים בן יאשיהו
pairs.en: one who transgresses the words of Torah in public, like Jehoiakim son of Josiah

pairs.ja: מפר ברית זה המושך לו ערלה
pairs.en: 'who breaks the covenant'—this is one who draws his foreskin over himself
one who was not circumcised in his maturity

aligned.ja: והנאך קאלוא פי ג'מיע אלאשיא אלתי קאלוא אלחכמים פיהא אן פאעלהא אין לו חלק לעולם הבא קאלוא מה אנן קימין אם בשעשה תשובה אין לך דבר שעומד בפני בעל תשובה, אלא בשלא עשה תשובה ומת ביסורין, יעני אן קוהֵ תלך אלד'נוב אלתי ד'כרוא פיהא אין לו חלק לעולם הבא עלי סאיר אלד'נוב אן אליסורין מע אלמיתה לא תסתגפרהא.
aligned.en: And there they said, concerning all the things about which the Sages declared that whoever does them "has no portion in the World to Come": "How do we stand? If he repented, there is nothing that can stand before one who repents; rather, [it speaks] of one who did not repent and died amid sufferings"—meaning that, given the gravity of those sins about which they said "he has no portion in the World to Come" relative to other sins, even sufferings together with death do not procure atonement for them.

pairs.en: has no portion in the World to Come

pairs.ja: אין לך דבר שעומד בפני בעל תשובה
pairs.en: there is nothing that can stand before one who repents
one who did not repent and died amid sufferings
the gravity of those sins

aligned.ja: משנה [טו]
aligned.en: Mishnah [15]

aligned.ja: קלות, הי אלכ'פה. ונוח, אלתהדו ואלתת'בת. פקאל פי הד'ה אלוציה אד'א חצ'רת מע רג'ל כביר אלמנזלה פאג'על נפסך לה קל וצרף נפסך בין ידיה כיף שא, ואבד'ל נפסך לה.
aligned.en: *Qalut* is lightness, and *naḥat* is gentleness and steadiness. He said in this counsel: when you are in the presence of a man of high rank, make yourself slight before him, conduct yourself before him however he wishes, and give yourself over to him.

pairs.en: *Qalut* is lightness
*naḥat* is gentleness and steadiness
a man of high rank
make yourself slight before him
give yourself over to him

aligned.ja: ואד'א חצ'רת מע רג'ל אסוד אלשער יעני פתי אלסן פלא תפעל כד'לך בל תוקר מעה ולא תסתרסל ולא תנבסט.
aligned.en: But when you are in the presence of a man with black hair—that is, young in years—do not act thus; rather, comport yourself with dignity toward him and do not abandon restraint or grow overly familiar.

pairs.ja: רג'ל אסוד אלשער יעני פתי אלסן
pairs.en: a man with black hair—that is, young in years
do not act thus
comport yourself with dignity toward him
do not abandon restraint or grow overly familiar

aligned.ja: ת'ם קאל לא תט'ן אן אלד'י נהיתך מן אלאנבסאט מע צגיר אלסן יוג'ב אן תלקאה בעבוסה ווג'ה מקטב, ליס ד'לך אלגרץ', בל ינבגי אן תלקי אלנאס כלהם צגירהם וכבירהם, אלחר מנהם ואלעבד כל שכ'ץ מן נוע אלאנסאן בסרור ופרח, והד'א אכת'ר מן קול שמאי בסבר פנים יפות.
aligned.en: Then he said: do not suppose that, by forbidding you familiarity with the young, he means that you must meet such a one with a scowl and a frowning face. That is not the intent; rather, you ought to meet all people—young and old, free and slave, every individual of the human kind—with cheerfulness and joy. This goes beyond Shammai's saying, "with a pleasant countenance" (Avot 1:15).

pairs.ja: לא תט'ן אן אלד'י נהיתך מן אלאנבסאט
pairs.en: do not suppose that, by forbidding you familiarity
you must meet such a one with a scowl and a frowning face

pairs.ja: תלקי אלנאס כלהם צגירהם וכבירהם, אלחר מנהם ואלעבד
pairs.en: you ought to meet all people—young and old, free and slave
with cheerfulness and joy
Shammai's saying, "with a pleasant countenance"

aligned.ja: משנה [טז]
aligned.en: Mishnah [16]

aligned.ja: מסורת, חפט' אלוצאיא. יקול אן אד'א נדר אלאנסאן נדרים עלי אשיא ות'בתהא פתחצל לה מלכהֵ אלתמנע ממא שא אן ימתנע מנה, פית'בת לה ויסהל עליה אלפרישות אעני אלתחפט' מן אלטמאות כמא קאלוא פי חגיגה בגדי עמי הארץ מדרס לפרושים.
aligned.en: *Masoret* [means] the keeping of the precepts. He says that if a person makes vows concerning [various] matters and holds firm to them, there is formed in him a disposition of abstaining from whatever he wishes to abstain from; and there becomes established for him, and made easy for him, *perishut*—I mean the guarding of oneself from impurities, as they said in [tractate] Ḥagigah: "The garments of an ʿam ha-aretz are a source of *midras*-impurity for *perushim*" (M. Ḥagigah 2:7).

pairs.en: *Masoret* [means] the keeping of the precepts
a person makes vows concerning [various] matters
there is formed in him a disposition of abstaining
*perishut*—I mean the guarding of oneself from impurities
The garments of an ʿam ha-aretz are a source of *midras*-impurity for *perushim*

aligned.ja: משנה [יז]
aligned.en: Mishnah [17]

aligned.ja: יקול אן תעריף אלד'י אפצ'ל עליה בקדר אלפצ'ילה הו אפצ'אל אכ'ר, לאנה קד יפצ'ל עלי אלשכ'ץ רחמה לה ולא יערפה בקדר מא עמל מעה אסתקלאל לחקה.
aligned.en: He says that to acknowledge the one you have benefited according to the measure of the favor is itself a further favor; for one may bestow a benefit upon a person out of mercy for him and not acknowledge it according to the extent of what he did with him—out of slighting his due.

pairs.ja: תעריף אלד'י אפצ'ל עליה בקדר אלפצ'ילה
pairs.en: to acknowledge the one you have benefited according to the measure of the favor
is itself a further favor
bestow a benefit upon a person out of mercy for him

pairs.ja: ולא יערפה בקדר מא עמל מעה
pairs.en: not acknowledge it according to the extent of what he did with him
out of slighting his due

aligned.ja: משנה [יח]
aligned.en: Mishnah [18]

aligned.ja: הד'א אלפצל תצ'מן אגראץ' עט'ימה ג'דא, ולא יכון מת'ל הד'א אלכלאם אלא לר' עקיבה והד'א שרחה באיג'אז. ובשרט אן תפהם מא תקדם פי אלפצול אלמתקדמה.
aligned.en: This section embraces exceedingly great themes, and a discourse such as this could belong to none but Rabbi Akiva. Here is its interpretation in brief, on the condition that you grasp what was set down in the foregoing sections.

pairs.en: exceedingly great themes

pairs.ja: לא יכון מת'ל הד'א אלכלאם אלא לר' עקיבה
pairs.en: a discourse such as this could belong to none but Rabbi Akiva
its interpretation in brief

pairs.ja: תפהם מא תקדם פי אלפצול אלמתקדמה
pairs.en: you grasp what was set down in the foregoing sections

aligned.ja: קאל כל מא פי אלעאלם מעלום ענדה תעלי והו ידרכה והו קולה הכל צפוי.
aligned.en: He said: everything in the world is known to Him, exalted, and He apprehends it—this is his statement, "All is foreseen."

pairs.ja: כל מא פי אלעאלם מעלום ענדה תעלי
pairs.en: everything in the world is known to Him, exalted
He apprehends it
All is foreseen

aligned.ja: ת'ם קאל ולא תט'ן אן בכונה תעלי יעלם אלאפעאל ילזם אלג'בר ואן יכון אלאנסאן מקהור עלי עמל מן אלאעמאל, ליס אלאמר כד'לך, בל כל שכ'ץ מכ'יר פי מא יפעלה והו קולה והרשות נתונה, יעני רשות כל אדם נתונה לו עלי מא בינא פי אלפצל אלת'אמן.
aligned.en: Then he said: do not suppose that, by His, exalted, knowing the deeds, compulsion follows, and that a person is coerced in some deed among his deeds. The matter is not so; rather, every individual has free choice in what he does—this is his statement, "and freedom is granted," meaning "the freedom of every person is granted to him," as we explained in the eighth section [of the Eight Chapters].

pairs.ja: בכונה תעלי יעלם אלאפעאל ילזם אלג'בר
pairs.en: by His, exalted, knowing the deeds, compulsion follows

pairs.ja: אלאנסאן מקהור עלי עמל מן אלאעמאל
pairs.en: a person is coerced in some deed among his deeds

pairs.ja: כל שכ'ץ מכ'יר פי מא יפעלה
pairs.en: every individual has free choice in what he does
freedom is granted
the freedom of every person is granted to him
we explained in the eighth section

aligned.ja: קאל ומחאכמהֵ אללה לאלנאס אנמא הי באחסאן לא בתקצי אלחק אלואג'ב עליהם כמא בין תעלי מן אוצאפה וקאל ארך אפים ורב חסד, קאלוא ארך אפים לצדיקים ולרשעים, וקאל אלנבי ואצף טוב ה' לכל.
aligned.en: He said: and God's judgment of people is according to grace, not according to the strict exaction of the right owed by them—as He, exalted, made clear among His attributes when He said, "long-suffering and abounding in lovingkindness" (Exod 34:6). They said: "'long-suffering'—toward both the righteous and the wicked." And the Prophet said, in describing [Him], "The Lord is good to all" (Ps 145:9).

pairs.en: God's judgment of people
is according to grace
not according to the strict exaction of the right owed by them
long-suffering and abounding in lovingkindness
'long-suffering'—toward both the righteous and the wicked
The Lord is good to all

aligned.ja: ת'ם קאל אן אלפצ'איל ליס תחצל בקדר עט'מהֵ אלעמל בל בכת'רהֵ עדד אלעמל, וד'לך אן אלפצ'איל אנמא תחצל בתכריר אפעאל אלכ'יר מראת עדידה ובד'לך תחצל אלמלכה, לא באן יפעל אלנסאן פעלא ואחדא עט'ימא מן אפעאל אלכ'יר, לאן ד'לך וחדה ליס תחצל בה מלכה.
aligned.en: Then he said that the virtues are attained not according to the magnitude of the deed but according to the great number of deeds; for the virtues are attained only through the repetition of good acts many times, and by this the disposition is formed—not by a person's performing a single great act among the good acts, for that alone forms no disposition.

pairs.ja: אלפצ'איל ליס תחצל בקדר עט'מהֵ אלעמל
pairs.en: the virtues are attained not according to the magnitude of the deed
but according to the great number of deeds
through the repetition of good acts many times
by this the disposition is formed

pairs.ja: לא באן יפעל אלנסאן פעלא ואחדא עט'ימא
pairs.en: not by a person's performing a single great act

aligned.ja: מת'ל ד'לך אן אלאנסאן אד'א והב למסתחק אלף דינאר פי חין ואחד ולשכ'ץ ואחד, ליס תחצל לה פצ'ילהֵ אלכרם בהד'א אלפעל אלואחד אלעט'ים כמת'ל מא תחצל למן כרם אלף מרה באלף דינאר ודפע כל דינאר מנהא בוג'ה כרם, לאן הד'א תכרר מנה פעל אלכרם אלף מרה פחצלת מלכה קויה, והד'א מרה ואחדה פקט נזעת אלנפס נזועא עט'ימא לפעל כ'יר ת'ם כפת ען ד'לך.
aligned.en: An example: if a person gives a thousand dinars to a worthy recipient at a single moment and to a single individual, the virtue of generosity is not formed in him by this one great act as it is formed in one who acted generously a thousand times with a thousand dinars, disbursing each of those dinars in a manner of generosity—because in the latter the act of generosity was repeated a thousand times, so that a strong disposition was formed, whereas in the former, on one occasion only, the soul stirred itself with a great impulse toward a good act and then desisted from it.

pairs.ja: והב למסתחק אלף דינאר פי חין ואחד
pairs.en: gives a thousand dinars to a worthy recipient at a single moment
the virtue of generosity
acted generously a thousand times with a thousand dinars

pairs.ja: תכרר מנה פעל אלכרם אלף מרה
pairs.en: the act of generosity was repeated a thousand times
a strong disposition was formed

pairs.ja: נזעת אלנפס נזועא עט'ימא לפעל כ'יר ת'ם כפת ען ד'לך
pairs.en: the soul stirred itself with a great impulse toward a good act and then desisted from it

aligned.ja: וכד'לך פי אלשריעה ליס אג'ר מן אפדי אסירא במאיהֵ דינאר או תצדק עלי צ'עיף במאיה דינאר כאנת די מחסורו מת'ל מן אפדי עשרה אסרא או אכמל נקצאן עשרה צ'עפא ולו בעשרה דנאניר. ועלי הד'א פקס, והד'א הו מעני קולה לפי רוב המעשה לא על פי המעשה.
aligned.en: So too in the Law: there is no reward for one who redeems a captive with a hundred dinars or gives charity to a needy man with a hundred dinars—that this should be "what he lacks" (Deut 15:8)—equal to one who redeems ten captives, or supplies the want of ten needy persons, even with [only] ten dinars. By this measure judge [the rest]. This is the meaning of his saying, "according to the abundance of the deed, and not according to the [magnitude of the] deed."

pairs.en: redeems a captive with a hundred dinars
gives charity to a needy man
one who redeems ten captives
supplies the want of ten needy persons

pairs.ja: לפי רוב המעשה לא על פי המעשה
pairs.en: according to the abundance of the deed, and not according to the [magnitude of the] deed

aligned.ja: משנה [יט]
aligned.en: Mishnah [19]

aligned.ja: מקיף, ימהל באלדין ולא יטלבה עלי אלמקאם. והד'א אלמת'ל בין מעלום, ואלגרץ' בקולה וכל הרוצה ללות בא ולוה יוכד אלגרץ' אלמתקדם אן ליס ת'ם ג'בר ולא קהר, בל באכ'תיאר אלאנסאן יפעל מא שא מן אפעאלה.
aligned.en: *Maqqif* [means] one who grants a respite in the debt and does not demand it on the spot. This parable is clear and evident. By his saying, "and whoever wishes to borrow may come and borrow," the aforementioned theme is reinforced: that there is no compulsion or coercion, but rather that by his own free choice a person does whatever he does among his deeds.

pairs.ja: מקיף, ימהל באלדין ולא יטלבה עלי אלמקאם
pairs.en: *Maqqif* [means] one who grants a respite in the debt and does not demand it on the spot
This parable is clear and evident
whoever wishes to borrow may come and borrow
there is no compulsion or coercion
by his own free choice a person does whatever he does

aligned.ja: וקולה והגבאין מחזרין, הו מת'ל ען אלמות וסאיר אלעקובאת אלנאזלה באלאנסאן. והכל מתוקן לסעודה, אן הד'א כלה אלגאיה מנה חיי העולם הבא.
aligned.en: And his saying, "and the collectors make their rounds," is a parable for death and the other punishments that befall a person. And "all is prepared for the banquet"—the whole purpose of all this is the life of the World to Come.

pairs.en: the collectors make their rounds
a parable for death and the other punishments
that befall a person
all is prepared for the banquet
the whole purpose of all this is the life of the World to Come

aligned.ja: משנה [כ]
aligned.en: Mishnah [20]

aligned.ja: יריד בד'לך אן כל ואחד מנהמא מפיד פי וג'וד אלאכ'ר ומתמם לה. ואמא קולה פי אלבינה ואלדעת פהד'א מעני פלספי דקיק ג'דא, ואנא אד'כרה מתכלא עלי פהם מן נט'ר פי הד'א אלגרץ'.
aligned.en: He intends by this that each of the two is profitable for the existence of the other and brings it to completion. As for his statement concerning *binah* and *daʿat*, this is an extremely subtle philosophical matter, which I will mention while relying upon the understanding of one who has reflected upon this subject.

pairs.ja: כל ואחד מנהמא מפיד פי וג'וד אלאכ'ר
pairs.en: each of the two is profitable for the existence of the other
brings it to completion
his statement concerning *binah* and *daʿat*
an extremely subtle philosophical matter
one who has reflected upon this subject

aligned.ja: וד'לך אן הד'א אלעקל אלד'י יחצל לנא ונסתפידה אנמא הו אדראכנא אלמעקולאת אלתי נדרכהא, אמא באן ננתזע אלצורה ונעקלהא או נדרך אלצור אלמפארקה פי וג'ודהא דון אן נג'עלהא נחן עקלא, בל הי פי וג'ודהא עקל, והד'א אלאדראך הו אלד'י יתסמי בינה, והו אלעקל.
aligned.en: [The matter is this:] this intellect which comes to be in us and which we acquire is nothing other than our apprehension of the intelligibles that we apprehend—either by our abstracting a form and conceiving it, or by our apprehending the separate forms which in their very existence are without our making them intellect; rather, they are in their existence [already] intellect. This apprehension is what is called *binah*, and it is the intellect.

pairs.en: this intellect which comes to be in us and which we acquire
our apprehension of the intelligibles that we apprehend
by our abstracting a form and conceiving it
apprehending the separate forms
they are in their existence [already] intellect

pairs.ja: הד'א אלאדראך הו אלד'י יתסמי בינה
pairs.en: This apprehension is what is called *binah*

aligned.ja: ובאלעקל איצ'א נעקל וימכננא אן נדרך מא נדרך, פכאנה יקול אן לם נדרך מעקול פלא עקל לנא, פאן לם יכון לנא עקל פלא נדרך מעקול, לאן באלעקל נדרכה. ופהם הד'א עויץ ולו מן אלכתב אלמוצ'ועה לה פכיף מן הנא, ואנמא ארשדנא אליה ארשאדא פקט.
aligned.en: And by the intellect, too, we conceive, and it becomes possible for us to apprehend what we apprehend. It is as though he were saying: if we apprehend no intelligible, then we have no intellect; and if we have no intellect, then we apprehend no intelligible, since it is by the intellect that we apprehend it. Grasping this is difficult even from the books composed for it—how much more so from here; we have only directed you toward it as a mere pointing of the way.

pairs.ja: ובאלעקל איצ'א נעקל וימכננא אן נדרך
pairs.en: by the intellect, too, we conceive, and it becomes possible for us to apprehend

pairs.ja: אן לם נדרך מעקול פלא עקל לנא
pairs.en: if we apprehend no intelligible, then we have no intellect
it is by the intellect that we apprehend it

pairs.ja: עויץ ולו מן אלכתב אלמוצ'ועה לה
pairs.en: difficult even from the books composed for it
we have only directed you toward it as a mere pointing of the way

aligned.ja: משנה [כא]
aligned.en: Mishnah [21]

aligned.ja: קד שרחנא מעני הד'א אלכלאם פי הד'א אלפרק מן כלאם ר' חנינה בן דוסא.
aligned.en: We have already explained the meaning of this statement in this very chapter, in connection with the words of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa.

pairs.en: We have already explained the meaning of this statement
in this very chapter

pairs.ja: מן כלאם ר' חנינה בן דוסא
pairs.en: in connection with the words of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa
